answer.decision: Choose regional token buckets with bounded global quotas and local burst allowance.
answer.action: Deploy one highly available limiter system in each region. Derive conservative regional shares from regionally replicated tenant entitlements, enforce per-tenant token buckets near request handling, and size burst capacity for short bursts up to 4× the five-minute average. During limiter or network failures, use a strictly bounded local fallback allowance rather than unrestricted fail-open behavior. Reconcile regional usage asynchronously and alert on sustained imbalance or overshoot.
reasons: Per-tenant regional enforcement isolates heavy tenants and protects shared capacity; the largest 2% generate 61% of peak request volume.
Regional request-path decisions avoid the 180 ms p99 latency and availability coupling of synchronous cross-region enforcement.
A calibrated burst allowance reduces costly false throttling during observed bursts lasting less than 20 seconds.
Bounded regional shares and fallback allowances keep requests flowing during partitions while limiting global quota overshoot.
The design can reuse regionally replicated entitlement data and requires only one new stateful limiter technology.
A centralized global limiter would be a latency and availability bottleneck, while uncoordinated per-instance buckets could multiply effective quotas as instances scale.
assumptions: The dependency budget permits one limiter technology deployed highly available across the three regions.
A small, explicitly bounded quota overshoot during partitions is acceptable.
Regional quota shares can be adjusted from observed traffic without requiring synchronous global coordination.
Application instances can maintain a small, bounded fallback allowance for temporary regional limiter failures.
risks: Traffic shifting rapidly between regions can cause false throttling when a tenant exhausts one regional share despite unused quota elsewhere.
Burst capacity, asynchronous reconciliation, and fallback allowances can produce bounded global overshoot.
Incorrectly sized fallback allowances could either weaken isolation or reject too much traffic during an outage.
The limiter may become a regional bottleneck unless it is sharded, replicated, capacity-tested, and monitored.
Regional allocation and reconciliation add operational complexity for the five-person platform team.

citations.claim: The top 2% of tenants generate 61% of peak request volume, making per-tenant isolation important.
Bursts frequently reach 4× a tenant's five-minute average for less than 20 seconds, supporting a short local burst allowance.
Cross-region control-plane round trips have 180 ms p99 latency, disfavoring synchronous global enforcement.
A previous regional dependency outage lasted 11 minutes while application instances remained healthy, supporting bounded local fallback behavior.
The platform team has capacity for at most one new stateful dependency.
Regionally replicated entitlement data can provide per-tenant quota inputs without a new global lookup.
